newsitem.title: USA: Dow the market darling in quiet pre-holiday trade.
newsitem.headline: Dow the market darling in quiet pre-holiday trade.

text.p: The Dow Industrials rose as investors continued to favor big name stocks with high dividends in the shortened session Tuesday before the Christmas holiday.
The Dow was up about 25 to 6513 in late morning trading about midway through the session, beating most other major indexes which were lightly higher.
The New York Stock Exchange, Nasdaq and the American Stock Exchange will close at 1300 EST/1800 GMT Tuesday and will be closed Wednesday, December 25.
The Dow 30 was up nearly 0.4 percent. The Standard & Poor's 500 Index of large companies was also performing well, up 0.24 percent or 1.82 to 748.74.

The Nasdaq Composite Index and Russell 2000 Indexes were also positive but sharply trailed the indexes of major companies. The Nasdaq was only a trace higher, up 0.24 to 1279.76. The Russell 2000 Index of small cap stocks was up 0.15, or 0.04 percent, to 355.57.
Volume was very light, with many investors heading home early for the holidays. About 85 million shares had traded on the New York Stock Exchange at late morning.

"Bonds are stable, which gives the market some hope ... Without any movement in interest rates, there isn't much downside because there's no changes in fundamentals," said Edgar Peters, chief investment strategist at Boston-based PanAgora Asset Management Inc.
He said stocks with high-yield dividends would continue to be attractive as long as bond yields remained low.

"If bond yields go up, we could see some fireworks. I expect that to happen sometime next year, depending on the fed," he said, citing a recent rise in capacity utiliztion increasing and low unemployemnt.

Utility stocks were faring well, with the NYSE Utilities component up 1.46, or almost 0.60 percent, to 257.93. Analysts said investors might be still be favoring late-cycle market sectors in a defensive play.

Several Dow components rose. AT&T Corp rose 1-1/4 to 41-1/4 on light volume after a bullish comment in the Wall Street Journal on its management style and energy of John Walter, its new COO and CEO designate.
American Express added 2-1/2 to 59-3/8, Philip Morris Cos Inc rose 1-1/2 to 114-1/2, and IBM Corp added 1-1/8 to 155-1/4.

In some special situations, Zitel Inc shares surged in morning trading on a combination of a short squeeze and rumored investing by financier George Soros. The shares rose as high as 50-1/2, a new year high, before settling back to its opening price of 45-3/4.

TRO Learning Inc shares lost almost half their value after it said fiscal 1996 fourth quarter revenues and profits fell short of expectations and that, as a result of the lower earnings, the company is in noncompliance with its loan agreement. Shares fell 8-3/4 to 8-3/4.
